01PROJECT-BASED COURSEExpert Knowledge Extraction & StructuringDevelop your team’s ability to uncover critical expertise and turn it into knowledge others can use.+

Experts often know more than they can explain in a general interview. This course trains employees to elicit tacit knowledge, explore real situations and organize the findings into clear knowledge items. Participants select an expert and a real knowledge challenge, then apply the methods between sessions. Throughout the course, participants work toward a completed knowledge retention project, developing internal expertise while creating a resource their organization can use.

For Knowledge professionals, HR and learning teams, and employees selected to lead expert knowledge projects.

Plan this course for your team

Learning focus

  • Recognize different layers of explicit and tacit knowledge.
  • Use expert interviews, real cases and targeted questions.
  • Extract reasoning, practical know-how and decision criteria.
  • Structure findings into connected knowledge items that others can learn from.
  • Apply the methods to a real expert knowledge retention project.

Applied work An expert knowledge project developed during the course.

02COURSE & WORKSHOPExpert Knowledge TransferHelp experts share their experience in ways others can learn from, and help colleagues ask the questions that matter.+

Knowing how to perform a task does not automatically make that knowledge easy to share. Experts may skip steps that feel obvious, rely on professional shorthand or struggle to explain their judgment. This program helps experts recognize what they take for granted and make their knowledge accessible to colleagues. It also addresses the knowledge gaps that persist after a handover, helping teams connect learning from experts with mentoring, role transitions and practical learning resources.

For Experts, mentors, managers and teams responsible for succession and knowledge transfer.

Plan this program for your experts

Learning focus

  • Recognize what an expert takes for granted.
  • Surface tacit knowledge through questions and examples.
  • Explain professional reasoning in language others can understand and apply.
  • Choose suitable written, visual and digital learning resources.
  • Build a knowledge base that supports handover and mentoring.

Applied work A structured transfer plan for a real role or area of expertise.

03MANAGEMENT COURSEKnowledge Management for ManagersMake knowledge management a practical part of how you lead, improve performance and protect continuity.+

This course gives managers a practical understanding of knowledge management and how it supports organizational performance. Participants examine how relevant knowledge is organized, how it reaches employees and how experience becomes a resource for future work. Practical tools help managers retain knowledge, learn from experts, capture project insights and share knowledge through everyday work routines. Exercises connect the material with each manager’s own organizational challenge, making the learning relevant to decisions they already need to make.

For Business leaders, department and team managers, and HR managers.

Develop your managers’ KM capabilities

Learning focus

  • Connect knowledge needs with business priorities.
  • Organize and maintain a relevant knowledge core.
  • Capture insights and useful practices from projects and events.
  • Retain knowledge and strengthen learning from experts.
  • Integrate knowledge sharing into management routines.

Applied work Practical actions for a knowledge challenge in the manager’s team.

04FOUNDATIONS & PRACTICE COURSEKnowledge Champions TrainingPrepare the people who will lead knowledge management activities and develop capability across your organization.+

Knowledge champions need a broad view of the field and practical tools they can use with their colleagues. This program introduces knowledge management and develops the skills to assess current practices, map critical knowledge and build a knowledge core: an organized body of knowledge that supports the work. Participants learn how to organize knowledge using a taxonomy, capture and retain knowledge, and encourage learning from experts. The aim is to develop people who can turn knowledge management into an ongoing organizational practice.

For Designated knowledge champions, knowledge coordinators and emerging KM leaders.

Build your network of knowledge champions

Learning focus

  • Understand the principles and scope of knowledge management.
  • Use diagnostic tools and a knowledge matrix.
  • Create a knowledge core with a practical taxonomy.
  • Apply tools for knowledge capture and retention.
  • Encourage sharing and learning from experts.

Applied work A knowledge map and initial plan for the champion’s area of responsibility.

05PRACTICAL COURSE & WORKSHOPKnowledge Capture in the Flow of WorkCapture what people learn throughout the employee lifecycle and at each stage of a project.+

Useful knowledge emerges while people are doing the work. This training explores how to capture it through routines that teams already use: onboarding, mentoring, debriefs and after-action reviews, project learning and employee departures. Participants learn to ask questions that reveal practical insights and tacit knowledge, structure what they find and make it available to the next person who needs it. The program connects individual experience with a knowledge base that can keep developing over time.

For HR and learning teams, project leaders, mentors, managers and knowledge champions.

Bring knowledge capture into daily work

Learning focus

  • Onboarding: identify what a new employee needs to learn.
  • Mentoring: capture the reasoning behind expert guidance.
  • Debriefs: turn experience into lessons through structured reflection.
  • Projects: capture insights while they are still fresh.
  • Employee departure: structure handovers and capture knowledge before someone leaves.

Applied work A knowledge capture routine for a relevant work process or employee transition.

06CHANGE & ADOPTION TRAININGChange Management & AdoptionHelp people adopt new knowledge practices, ways of working and KM technologies.+

Introducing a new system or approach changes how people work. This training examines the emotional responses that change can produce and the connection between human psychology and technology adoption. It introduces models and methods for embedding change, with a focus on the people who will use the new system or adopt the new practice. For a knowledge management initiative, this means considering adoption alongside the technology and the process from the outset.

For Managers, HR professionals, KM teams and IT leaders introducing new systems or work practices.

Support adoption of your KM initiative

Learning focus

  • Understand emotional responses to organizational change.
  • Connect psychology with technology adoption.
  • Explore models and methods for embedding change.
  • Apply the learning to a new system, concept or work practice.

Applied work An approach to supporting adoption in your own change initiative.

RESEARCHER · PRACTITIONER · EDUCATOR

MEET DR. DAN ASHER

The person behind
the practice.

Dan combines research into tacit knowledge, years of organizational leadership and hands-on work with experts across professions.

Before leading his consulting practice, Dan served as a knowledge management and learning innovation leader in a government organization. His experience spans management, organizational learning and the interpersonal skills needed to understand people’s work and help them share what they know.

His doctoral research at the University of Haifa focused on tacit knowledge in professions that rely on interpersonal interaction. He explored how expert knowledge can be elicited and structured to address organizational knowledge loss. His two research articles examine the layers of tacit knowledge and ways to elicit expertise from interpersonal interactions.

Dan has worked with more than 100 experts on knowledge extraction projects. He describes himself as a “pracademic”: someone who connects theory with organizational practice. His work combines curiosity about people and technology with a practical interest in how knowledge supports real decisions.

Teaching your people to do the work

Dan co-created and led sessions in the Knowledge Management Global Network’s 2024 online course, “Leveraging the Value Creation of Tacit Knowledge.” His courses connect methods with participants’ actual organizational challenges. In the extraction course, employees work with an expert and develop a knowledge retention project as they learn. His advisory work complements this training with organizational assessments and KM technology requirements.

At Israel Aerospace Industries, an expert knowledge project developed into a broader engineering knowledge initiative, connecting a structured knowledge core with a generative AI assistant.

A FEW COMMON QUESTIONS

Before we start.

Is this relevant only when experts retire?+

Retirement is one reason to capture expert knowledge. The same work can support role changes, succession, onboarding, everyday learning and the development of knowledge resources for AI. Capturing expertise while it is still in use gives others time to learn from it and test it in practice.

What if experts find it difficult to explain what they know?+

That is one of the main reasons to use a structured extraction process. We explore real cases, decisions, observations and examples to uncover knowledge that may not emerge in a general interview or in response to a request to write a manual.

Can you work with our existing KM platforms?+

Yes. We assess the current environment and define how knowledge should be organized, found, shared and maintained. Where appropriate, this includes requirements for SharePoint and Microsoft 365 and coordination with your IT team or technology provider.

How does expert knowledge contribute to generative AI?+

Expert knowledge can add reasoning, exceptions and context that are absent from existing documents. We help structure and validate those knowledge assets, document their sources and connect them with the intended AI use case. We also define how to validate and maintain the knowledge and review the resulting AI outputs.

Can our own team learn to do this?+

Yes. Practical courses and workshops help your employees develop the skills to elicit, structure and transfer knowledge. Programs can be built around a real expert knowledge project, so participants create useful resources for their organization as they learn.
